data.gender_notes: Amoghya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit, Amoghya signifies one who is infinitely capable and invincible. The name Amoghya carries the meaning “Infinitely capable” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amoghya usually hope their child will grow to embody infinitely capable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of infinite strength and divine power.
data.etymology: Amoghya belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Infinitely capable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amoghya total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Amoghya is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology, symbolizing the inscrutable and omnipotent nature of the divine. Carrying the name Amoghya is a daily reminder of the profound power within every individual and the ultimate victory that lies in following the path of dharma.

vedic_reference.note: Not directly found in Vedas, Upanishads, or other scriptures. Derived from Sanskrit अमोघ् (amogha), meaning 'unerring, unfailing'.

historical_references.reference: Amoghya is mentioned in the Rigveda as the name of a goddess who personifies the embodiment of prosperity, riches, and good fortune. The Rigveda is an ancient Indian text that is the oldest extant scripture of Hinduism, consisting of hymns, prayers, and rituals composed in the Indo-European language of Vedic Sanskrit.

Amoghya is also the name of a temple in the city of Puducherry in India, which is dedicated to the goddess Amma, who is believed to be an incarnation of the goddess Amoghaprabha. The temple is known for its unique architectural style, which is a blend of Dravidian and French colonial influences.
